memories.content: Docker containers package applications with their dependencies into portable units that run consistently across environments. Use docker build to create an image, then docker run to launch a container instance.
Docker networking enables container-to-container communication via bridge networks. Use docker network create for custom networks with DNS resolution between containers.
Docker volumes persist data beyond container lifecycle. Use named volumes for managed storage and bind mounts for development. Never store state inside containers.
Container security best practices: use non-root users, scan images for vulnerabilities with Trivy, implement network policies, and avoid running as root in production.
Docker Compose defines multi-container applications with docker-compose.yml. Use depends_on for startup ordering, volumes for persistence, and networks for isolation.
Docker multi-stage builds reduce final image size by copying only necessary artifacts from builder stages. Use AS builder to separate build and runtime dependencies.
Docker HEALTHCHECK instruction monitors container health. Configure interval, timeout, and retries for automatic restart on failure. Essential for orchestration.
Docker debugging: use docker exec for interactive shells, docker logs for output, docker inspect for metadata, and docker cp to copy files in/out of containers.
Docker resource limits prevent container resource exhaustion. Set CPU and memory limits in docker-compose or Kubernetes resource quotas to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
Docker cleanup: use docker system prune to remove unused containers, images, and networks. Schedule regular cleanup in CI to prevent disk bloat.
Python pytest enables test-driven development with fixtures, parametrize decorators, and assertion rewriting. Use conftest.py for shared fixtures across test modules.
Python asyncio enables concurrent I/O operations using coroutines. Use async/await syntax with asyncio.gather for parallel execution of async functions.
Python decorators modify function behavior using @syntax. Common patterns include @lru_cache for memoization, @retry for resilience, and @property for getters.
Python context managers use with-statement for resource management. Implement __enter__ and __exit__ or use contextlib.contextmanager for generator-based context managers.
Python generators use yield to produce values lazily. Generator expressions provide memory-efficient iteration over large datasets without loading everything into memory.
Python dataclasses reduce boilerplate for data containers. Use @dataclass decorator with field() for default values, metadata, and frozen instances.
Python type hints improve code clarity and enable static analysis with mypy. Use Union for optional types, Protocol for structural subtyping, and TypeVar for generics.
Python error handling uses try/except/finally with specific exception types. Use custom exceptions for domain-specific errors and exception chaining with raise from.
Python regex with re module provides pattern matching. Use raw strings r'' for patterns, compiled patterns for reuse, and named groups for readable matches.
Python serialization: json for text, pickle for binary, dataclasses.asdict for dataclass conversion, and pydantic for validation-aware serialization.
Python concurrency: threading for I/O-bound work, multiprocessing for CPU-bound, asyncio for event-driven. Use ThreadPoolExecutor for simple parallelism.
Python memoization with functools.lru_cache caches function results. Use maxsize for cache bounds and typed=True for type-aware caching across different argument types.
Python encoding: use UTF-8 by default, encode/decode explicitly for bytes, handle BOM for cross-platform files, and use errors='replace' for unknown encodings.
Python imports use absolute or relative paths. Use __all__ to define public API, __init__.py for packages, and importlib for dynamic imports.
Python 3.10+ pattern matching with match/case provides structural pattern matching. Use | for alternatives, captures for variables, and guards for conditions.
Python generics with TypeVar enable type-safe container classes. Use Protocol for structural subtyping, bound TypeVar for constraints, and Generic for base classes.
Python metaclasses control class creation. Use __new__ for instance creation, __init__ for initialization, and __prepare__ for namespace customization.
Python unit testing with pytest uses fixtures for setup, parametrize for data-driven tests, marks for categorization, and monkeypatch for dependency injection.
Python type checking with mypy catches errors at development time. Use strict mode, TypedDict for dict schemas, and Literal for specific value constraints.
Python async patterns: asyncio.gather for parallel, asyncio.Queue for producer-consumer, asyncio.Semaphore for concurrency limits, asyncio.wait for timeouts.
Git branching workflows: trunk-based for continuous delivery, feature-branch for isolation, gitflow for releases. Use conventional commits for automated changelogs.
PostgreSQL transactions ensure ACID compliance. Use BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK with isolation levels: READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE.
PostgreSQL indexing: B-tree for equality/range, GIN for full-text/array, GiST for geometric. Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to identify missing indexes and sequential scans.
SQL optimization: use EXPLAIN ANALYZE for query plans, avoid N+1 queries, leverage covering indexes, and push predicates down to reduce rows scanned.
SQL joins: INNER JOIN for matching rows, LEFT JOIN for all from left, RIGHT JOIN for all from right, CROSS JOIN for cartesian product, self-join for hierarchical data.
Redis provides in-memory caching for session storage, rate limiting, leaderboards. Use EXPIRE for TTL, Pipeline for batching, and Lua scripts for atomic operations.
Redis Pub/Sub enables real-time messaging. Use SUBSCRIBE for channels, PUBLISH for broadcasting, and patterns for channel matching. Not durable — use Streams for persistence.
Kubernetes deployments manage pod replicas with rolling updates, rollback capability, and health checks. Use kubectl rollout for deployment management.
Kubernetes services provide stable network endpoints. ClusterIP for internal, NodePort for external, LoadBalancer for cloud, and ExternalName for CNAME aliases.
Kubernetes ingress manages external HTTP access. Configure TLS termination, path-based routing, rate limiting, and CORS with ingress annotations.
Kubernetes ConfigMaps store non-sensitive config. Mount as volumes or environment variables. Use from-file for existing configs, from-literal for inline values.
Helm charts package Kubernetes apps with templated manifests. Use values.yaml for config, Chart.yaml for metadata, and hooks for lifecycle management.
Kubernetes RBAC controls resource access. Define Roles (namespace-scoped) and ClusterRoles (cluster-wide), bind to users/groups/service accounts.
Kubernetes networking: pods get IP addresses, Services provide stable endpoints, NetworkPolicies control traffic flow, and CNI plugins handle pod-to-pod networking.
Kubernetes PersistentVolumes provide durable storage. Use PVCs for dynamic provisioning, StorageClasses for different performance tiers, and StatefulSets for stateful apps.
Kubernetes monitoring: Prometheus for metrics, Grafana for visualization, kube-state-metrics for cluster state, and kubelet metrics for node health.
REST API design: consistent resource naming, proper HTTP methods, status codes, pagination, filtering, HATEOAS links, and versioning strategies.
GraphQL schemas define type-safe contracts. Use queries for reads, mutations for writes, subscriptions for real-time, and DataLoader for N+1 prevention.
WebSocket connections enable bidirectional real-time communication. Handle reconnection, heartbeats, and message buffering for reliable delivery.
Structured logging with JSON records enables observability. Include request IDs, severity, timestamps, and context. Use correlation IDs across services.
TCP/IP networking: TCP for reliable delivery, UDP for speed, DNS for name resolution, TLS for encryption. Understand the OSI model layers for debugging.
Microservices patterns: circuit breaker for resilience, saga for distributed transactions, CQRS for read/write separation, and event sourcing for audit trails.
Container security: scan images with Trivy/Snyk, use distroless base images, enforce read-only filesystems, drop capabilities, and use seccomp profiles.

Decision: we containerized all services using Docker for reproducible deployments across development, staging, and production environments.
Decision: we standardized on JSON for memory serialization to ensure cross-language compatibility and human-readable debugging.
Decision: we selected PostgreSQL for JSONB support, CTEs, window functions, and advanced indexing capabilities needed for complex queries.
Decision: we adopted Terraform for infrastructure-as-code to manage cloud resources declaratively with state management and plan/apply workflow.
Decision: we chose Prometheus + Grafana for metrics collection and visualization, with AlertManager for multi-channel alerting.

Decision: we implement daily automated PostgreSQL backups with 30-day retention, point-in-time recovery, and cross-region replication.
Decision: we chose RabbitMQ for task queue workloads with priority queues, dead letter exchanges, and consumer prefetch tuning.
Decision: we use NGINX as reverse proxy with round-robin distribution, health checks, rate limiting, and SSL termination.
Decision: write-through caching for consistency, cache-aside for read-heavy workloads, TTL-based invalidation, and cache warming for cold starts.
Decision: we enforce ruff for linting, pyright for type checking, bandit for security analysis, and pre-commit hooks for local validation.
Decision: we use black for auto-formatting and isort for import sorting to maintain consistent code style across the team.
Decision: we use Alembic for database schema migrations with automatic generation, rollback support, and branch-aware migration heads.
Decision: testing pyramid — unit tests at base (fast, many), integration in middle (moderate), E2E at top (slow, few). Target 80% unit coverage.
Decision: we use Sentry for real-time error aggregation with release tracking, user context, and performance monitoring.
Decision: we chose AWS for mature ecosystem, extensive services, compliance certifications, and global region availability.
Decision: we chose Kubernetes over Docker Swarm for larger ecosystem, better scaling, cloud provider support, and community.
Decision: we use conventional commits for automated changelog generation and semantic versioning for release management.
Decision: PagerDuty integration with escalation policies for critical alerts, Slack for warnings, and email for informational.
Decision: composite indexes for multi-column queries, partial indexes for filtered queries, and covering indexes to avoid table lookups.
Decision: we use Kong for rate limiting, authentication, request transformation, and analytics at the API edge.
Decision: OAuth 2.0 with JWT tokens, rate limiting, input validation, CORS policies, and API key management for all endpoints.

Project: automated dependency updates with Dependabot for security patches and Renovate for version upgrades.
Project: performance profiling with cProfile, py-spy for sampling, memory_profiler for leaks, and py-spy for production.
Project: automated documentation with Sphinx for Python, TypeDoc for TypeScript, and docstring linting in CI.
Project: on-call rotation with PagerDuty, runbook documentation, incident response, and blameless post-mortems.

Event sourcing captures all state changes as an immutable sequence of events. Enables temporal queries, audit trails, and event replay for debugging.
Command Query Responsibility Segregation separates read and write models. Write model optimizes for consistency, read model for query performance.
Circuit breaker pattern prevents cascade failures by tracking failure counts and opening the circuit after threshold. Half-open state allows probe requests.
Saga pattern manages distributed transactions via choreography or orchestration. Each step has a compensating transaction for rollback.
Backpressure prevents system overload by signaling producers to slow down. Use bounded queues, flow control, and adaptive rate limiting.
Consistent hashing distributes data across nodes with minimal redistribution when nodes join/leave. Used in caches, databases, and load balancers.
CAP theorem: distributed systems can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance. Most systems choose AP or CP.
Write-ahead log (WAL) ensures durability by writing changes to log before applying to data pages. Enables crash recovery and replication.
Materialized views precompute and store query results. Refresh periodically or on-demand. Trade storage for query performance.
Connection pooling reuses database connections to avoid overhead of establishing new connections. Tune min/max connections and idle timeout.
Python GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) prevents true parallel execution of threads. Use multiprocessing for CPU-bound work or asyncio for I/O-bound.
Docker layer caching reuses unchanged layers during builds. Order Dockerfile commands from least to most frequently changing for optimal caching.
Kubernetes pod scheduling considers resource requests, node selectors, affinity/anti-affinity, taints/tolerations, and topology spread constraints.
PostgreSQL VACUUM reclaims storage from dead tuples. AUTOVACUUM runs automatically; manual VACUUM FULL rewrites the entire table.
Redis eviction policies: noeviction, allkeys-lru, volatile-lru, allkeys-random, volatile-random, volatile-ttl. Choose based on access patterns.
JWT tokens have expiry claims (exp). Use short-lived access tokens (15min) with refresh token rotation for long-lived sessions.
TLS handshake: client hello, server hello + certificate, key exchange, finish. TLS 1.3 reduces round trips and removes weak ciphers.
DNS caching at multiple levels: browser, OS, resolver. TTL controls cache duration. DNS propagation delays can cause deployment issues.
CI pipelines automate testing on push, deploy on merge. Use GitHub Actions workflows with matrix testing, caching, and artifact publishing.
asyncio.gather runs multiple coroutines concurrently. Use return_exceptions=True to handle individual failures without canceling others.
Kubernetes rolling updates gradually replace pods. Configure maxSurge and maxUnavailable for controlled rollout with zero downtime.
PostgreSQL CTEs (Common Table Expressions) with WITH clause enable readable complex queries, recursive queries, and temporary result sets.
Redis Streams provide durable message queues with consumer groups. Use XADD to publish, XREADGROUP to consume, and XPENDING for monitoring.
Docker layer vulnerabilities: scan each layer with Trivy, use distroless bases, minimize layers, and pin base image digests.
PodDisruptionBudget limits voluntary disruptions during maintenance. Set minAvailable or maxUnavailable to ensure availability during node drains.
concurrent.futures provides ThreadPoolExecutor and ProcessPoolExecutor. Use as_completed for streaming results and wait for timeouts.
PostgreSQL table partitioning: range for time-series, list for categorical, hash for distribution. Improves query performance and maintenance.
StatefulSet provides stable network identity and persistent storage for stateful applications like databases and message queues.

Decision: we use gRPC for internal service-to-service communication with protocol buffers, streaming, and code generation.

Decision: we use Fluentd for log collection, Elasticsearch for storage, and Kibana for visualization in our logging pipeline.
Decision: we use Istio service mesh for mTLS, traffic management, observability, and policy enforcement across microservices.

Project: database migration tool with schema diff, dry-run, rollback, and branch-aware migration management.
Project: service discovery with Consul for health checking, DNS resolution, and dynamic service registration.
Project: distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry for request propagation, span collection, and trace visualization.
Idempotency ensures repeated requests produce same result. Use idempotency keys for POST, natural idempotency for PUT/DELETE.
Graceful degradation reduces functionality under load instead of failing completely. Serve cached responses, disable features, or return partial results.
Bulkhead pattern isolates components to prevent cascade failures. Separate connection pools, thread pools, and resource limits per dependency.
Memory leak detection: use tracemalloc for allocation tracking, objgraph for reference cycles, and memory_profiler for line-by-line profiling.
Connection timeouts: set connect timeout < read timeout, use exponential backoff for retries, and implement circuit breakers for repeated failures.
Python functools: lru_cache for memoization, partial for argument binding, reduce for accumulation, wraps for decorator preservation, total_ordering for comparison.
Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scales pods based on CPU, memory, or custom metrics. Configure min/max replicas and stabilization windows.
PostgreSQL JSONB for semi-structured data: GIN indexing, containment operators, path queries, and aggregation functions for flexible schemas.
Docker BuildKit enables parallel builds, build caching, secrets mounting, and SSH forwarding. Use # syntax for improved Dockerfiles.
Decision: we adopted OpenTelemetry for vendor-neutral instrumentation with traces, metrics, and logs in a unified pipeline.
Decision: we use Consul for service discovery, health checking, KV store, and service mesh with connect proxy.
Project: zero trust network with mutual TLS, identity-based access, micro-segmentation, and continuous verification.
Project: canary deployment with traffic splitting, automated rollback on error rate spikes, and metric-based promotion.
Eventual consistency guarantees all replicas converge to same state eventually. Trade immediate consistency for availability and partition tolerance.
Saga orchestration uses a central coordinator to manage transaction steps and compensations. Easier to reason about than choreography.
Sidecar pattern deploys helper processes alongside main application. Used for logging, monitoring, proxying, and configuration management.
Kubernetes ResourceQuotas limit namespace resource consumption. Set CPU, memory, and object count limits to prevent resource exhaustion.
Redis persistence: RDB snapshots for point-in-time recovery, AOF for durability, both for maximum safety. Trade performance for durability.
Frozen dataclasses enforce immutability. Use for value objects, configuration, and thread-safe shared state. hash=True for dict/set keys.
Kubernetes NetworkPolicies control pod-to-pod traffic. Default deny all, then allow specific ingress/egress rules by label selectors.
PostgreSQL full-text search with tsvector/tsquery, GIN indexes, ranking functions, and language-specific stemming.
Decision: we use Prometheus for metrics collection with pull model, PromQL for queries, and AlertManager for alerting.
Decision: we use ArgoCD for GitOps-based continuous delivery with declarative manifests and automated sync.
Project: automated certificate management with cert-manager, Let's Encrypt, and certificate rotation.
Project: multi-tenancy with namespace isolation, resource quotas, network policies, and tenant-aware data routing.
Circuit breaker states: closed (normal), open (failing, reject requests), half-open (probe with limited requests). Transition on failure/success counts.
Retry with exponential backoff: double delay between retries, add jitter to prevent thundering herd, set max retries and total timeout.
Token bucket rate limiting: tokens added at fixed rate, requests consume tokens, bucket has max capacity. Allows bursts up to bucket size.
CPU cache locality affects performance. Sequential access is faster than random. Use data-oriented design for cache-friendly algorithms.
I/O-bound tasks wait on network/disk — use async/threading. CPU-bound tasks compute heavily — use multiprocessing or C extensions.
Python abstract base classes (abc) define interfaces with @abstractmethod. Use for plugin systems, dependency inversion, and type checking.
Kubernetes CronJobs run scheduled tasks. Configure schedule with cron syntax, concurrencyPolicy, and failedJobsHistoryLimit.
PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows actual query execution plan. Look for sequential scans, nested loops, hash joins, and sort operations.
Docker secrets management: use Docker secrets in Swarm, Kubernetes Secrets, or external vaults. Never bake secrets into images.
Decision: we use ArgoCD for GitOps continuous delivery with auto-sync, health checks, and rollback capabilities.
Decision: we use Istio service mesh for mTLS, traffic management, and observability across our microservices.
Project: chaos testing with Litmus for controlled failure injection, game days, and resilience scorecards.
Project: migrate API gateway from custom NGINX config to Kong with plugin ecosystem and admin API.
Actor model: isolated actors communicate via messages, no shared state. Used in Erlang, Akka, and Python's multiprocessing.
Pub/sub broadcasts to all subscribers (fan-out). Queue delivers to one consumer (load balancing). Choose based on consumption pattern.
GC pressure from too many short-lived objects. Reduce allocations, use object pooling, and profile with tracemalloc to find hotspots.
TCP_NODELAY disables Nagle's algorithm, reducing latency for small messages. Essential for real-time applications and interactive protocols.
Python Protocol for structural subtyping. Define interfaces without inheritance. Use @runtime_checkable for isinstance checks.
Kubernetes pod lifecycle: Pending → Running → Succeeded/Failed. Use init containers for setup, postStart/preStop hooks for lifecycle management.
PostgreSQL views simplify complex queries. Regular views re-execute query each time. Materialized views cache results for performance.
Docker debugging: docker logs --follow, docker exec -it, docker inspect, docker stats, and docker system df for disk usage.
Decision: we use Cilium for eBPF-based networking, network policy enforcement, and Hubble for observability.
Decision: we use Backstage as developer portal for service catalog, templates, and documentation.
Project: internal developer platform with self-service provisioning, golden paths, and automated compliance.
Project: FinOps dashboard for cloud cost allocation, forecasting, optimization recommendations, and budget alerts.
Sidecar runs alongside app (logging, proxying). Ambassador proxies outbound connections (service discovery, TLS termination). Different responsibilities.
Strangler fig pattern gradually replaces legacy system by routing new features to modern implementation while legacy handles unchanged parts.
Cold start latency in serverless: minimize package size, use provisioned concurrency, keep functions warm with scheduled invocations.
Connection reuse with HTTP keep-alive reduces TCP/TLS overhead. Configure connection pools with appropriate max connections and idle timeout.
Python __slots__ restricts instance attributes, reducing memory overhead. Use for large numbers of instances. Incompatible with __dict__.
Pod topology spread constraints distribute pods across zones/nodes for high availability. Use maxSkew to control distribution balance.
PostgreSQL index types: B-tree (default), Hash (equality), GIN (arrays/full-text), GiST (geometric), BRIN (large ordered tables).
Docker build args pass variables during build. Use ARG for build-time, ENV for runtime. Multi-stage builds isolate build args from runtime.
Decision: we use Velero for Kubernetes cluster backup, restore, and disaster recovery with cloud storage integration.
Decision: we use Tekton for Kubernetes-native CI/CD pipelines with reusable tasks and cloud-events integration.
Project: platform engineering with golden paths, self-service APIs, and automated infrastructure provisioning.
Project: SRE practices with SLIs/SLOs, error budgets, toil reduction, and incident management automation.
Three pillars: metrics (numeric time series), logs (discrete events), traces (request paths). Together enable debugging distributed systems.
Chaos engineering principles: build hypothesis, run experiment, analyze results, improve. Start small, automate, and contain blast radius.
NUMA-awareness: memory access is faster within same NUMA node. Pin threads to nodes, allocate memory locally for performance-critical paths.
OS page cache caches file data in memory. Sequential reads are fast (cached), random reads may miss. Use mmap or direct I/O for large datasets.
Python walrus operator (:=) assigns and returns value in expressions. Useful in while loops, list comprehensions, and if conditions.
Kubernetes Endpoints objects hold IP addresses of pods backing a Service. EndpointSlice API provides scalable alternative for large services.
PostgreSQL sequences generate auto-incrementing integers. Use SERIAL (auto) or GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (SQL standard).
Docker security: run as non-root, use read-only root filesystem, drop all capabilities, add only needed ones, scan with Trivy.
Decision: we use Kyverno for Kubernetes policy management with validate, mutate, and generate policies in YAML.
Decision: we use OpenSearch for full-text search, log analytics, and observability with plugin ecosystem.
Project: zero-downtime database migration with dual-write, shadow reads, and gradual cutover.
Project: cost-per-query tracking for API endpoints with resource attribution and optimization recommendations.
Cell-based architecture isolates failures to bounded cells. Each cell handles a subset of users/requests with independent infrastructure.
Ambassador pattern proxies outbound connections. Handles service discovery, TLS termination, and retry logic away from application code.
SSD vs HDD: SSD for random I/O (databases, containers), HDD for sequential writes (logs, backups). IOPS difference is 100-1000x.
JVM warmup vs native startup: JVM has JIT optimization but slow cold start. GraalVM native-image for fast startup with AOT compilation.
Python enums with enum module: Enum for basic values, IntEnum for integer comparison, Flag for bit operations, auto() for sequential values.
DaemonSet runs one pod per node. Used for node-level agents: logging, monitoring, networking, storage drivers.
PostgreSQL locks: table-level, row-level, advisory. Use NOWAIT or SKIP LOCKED for concurrent updates. Deadlock detection with lock_timeout.
Docker Compose profiles enable optional services. Use profiles for dev-only tools, testing utilities, and debug containers.

Decision: we use Cilium for eBPF-based networking, network policy, and service mesh with Hubble observability.

Project: compliance automation with policy-as-code, automated audits, and evidence collection for SOC2/ISO27001.
Cell architecture: partition users into cells, each cell is independent failure domain. Limits blast radius of regional outages.
Queue-based load leveling absorbs traffic spikes. Producers enqueue requests, consumers process at sustainable rate. Prevents backend overload.
Container startup time: minimize layers, use distroless bases, pre-pull images, and avoid heavy initialization in entrypoint scripts.
DNS resolution latency: use connection keep-alive, cache DNS results, prefer IP literals for critical paths, and monitor DNS SLAs.
Python functools.cached_property computes value once then caches. Like property but lazy and cached. Thread-safe in Python 3.12+.
Pod disruption budgets ensure availability during voluntary disruptions. Set minAvailable or maxUnavailable for node drains and cluster upgrades.
PostgreSQL internal tables: pg_stat_activity (active queries), pg_locks (lock info), pg_stat_user_tables (table statistics).
Docker multi-architecture builds with buildx. Support amd64 and arm64 for Apple Silicon and cloud ARM instances.

Decision: we use Kyverno for Kubernetes admission control and policy enforcement with YAML-native policy definitions.

Project: cost allocation system with per-team/per-service attribution, chargeback reports, and optimization recommendations.
Adaptive rate limiting adjusts limits based on system load, error rates, and latency. Use AIMD (additive increase, multiplicative decrease).
Request coalescing deduplicates concurrent identical requests. First request fetches, others wait for result. Reduces backend load.
Thread pool sizing: CPU-bound = num_cores + 1, I/O-bound = num_cores * (1 + wait_time/service_time). Monitor queue depth and latency.
Connection pool sizing: too few = queuing, too many = resource exhaustion. Start with 2-4x CPU cores, tune based on latency and throughput.
Python contextlib: @contextmanager for generators, ExitStack for dynamic resources, suppress for exception handling, nullcontext for optional context.
Kubernetes readiness probes determine if pod can accept traffic. Failed readiness removes pod from Service endpoints. Essential for rolling updates.
PostgreSQL triggers fire on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Use for auditing, validation, derived data, and maintaining invariants.
Docker Compose watch mode auto-rebuilds on file changes. Use for development with hot-reload and live code updates.
Decision: we use Telegraf for metrics collection with 300+ input plugins and InfluxDB/Prometheus output.
Decision: we use Grafana Tempo for distributed tracing backend with object storage and TraceQL queries.
Project: SLO monitoring with SLI definition, error budget tracking, burn rate alerts, and automated incident response.
Project: data mesh implementation with domain-oriented ownership, data-as-a-product, and self-serve data platform.
CQRS + Event Sourcing: separate command/query models, persist events as source of truth, rebuild read models from event log.
Outbox pattern ensures reliable message publishing. Write event to outbox table in same transaction as business data, then publish asynchronously.
Memory alignment affects CPU cache performance. Struct packing, array-of-structs vs struct-of-arrays, and false sharing prevention.
System call overhead: context switches cost ~100ns-1μs. Batch syscalls, use io_uring for async I/O, and minimize kernel transitions.
Python dataclass field() for defaults, metadata, init control, and comparison exclusion. Use field(default_factory=list) for mutable defaults.
Kubernetes garbage collection: owning resources delete dependents. Use ownerReferences and foreground/background propagation policies.
PostgreSQL recursive CTEs with WITH RECURSIVE for hierarchical data: org charts, tree traversals, and graph queries.
Docker Compose override files (docker-compose.override.yml) extend base configuration. Use for environment-specific settings.
Decision: we use Victoria Metrics for long-term metrics storage with PromQL compatibility and cost-efficient compression.
Decision: we use OpenTelemetry Collector for vendor-neutral telemetry pipeline with processing and export flexibility.
Project: GitOps pipeline with ArgoCD, Kustomize overlays, and automated manifest generation from Helm charts.
Project: chaos game day platform for scheduling experiments, tracking results, and building resilience scorecards.
Backpressure mechanisms: bounded queues, credit-based flow control, adaptive rate limiting, and load shedding.
Idempotent receiver ensures duplicate message processing produces same result. Use message deduplication keys and idempotent operations.
NUMA locality: memory access within same NUMA node is 2-3x faster. Use numactl, CPU pinning, and local memory allocation.
